mainTopic: The husband's warning (קינוי) in the סוטה פסוקים: what the word means, why one witness is believed, and whether the warning is optional or required.
overview: The גמרא first finishes a discussion about the word קינוי, the husband's warning to his wife. Those who read it as 'anger' forbid the warning, while רב נחמן בר יצחק reads it as 'warning,' so it is permitted. Next come two lessons drawn from the סוטה פסוקים. רבי מאיר teaches that a sin done in secret is announced by הקדוש ברוך הוא in public, and ריש לקיש teaches that a person sins only when a spirit of foolishness (שטות) enters him. A ברייתא then explains that one witness is believed against a סוטה because her husband's warning and her seclusion already make the matter suspicious. אביי defends the order of events, warning first and then seclusion, by reading ועבר as 'it had already come.' The גמרא then concludes that the 'spirit' that moves a husband to warn his wife is a רוח טהרה. It proves this from a ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל calls the warning optional and רבי עקיבא calls it required. Finally, it shows that their disputes, about the warning and about a כהן becoming טמא for his sister, each come from reading a specific פסוק, not from one general rule.

steps.title: So these opinions hold that warning is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that ריש לקיש and רב יימר בר רבי שלמיה, who explained קינוי as a word of anger, must hold that a husband may not give his wife this warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems they hold that it is forbidden to give a warning (קינוי).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the explanations it just quoted. If קינוי means 'anger,' then these opinions must hold that it is forbidden to give such a warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, ריש לקיש and רב יימר בר רבי שלמיה explained the word קינוי as a word of anger. Stirring up anger is a bad trait, so the גמרא concludes that they forbid the husband from giving this warning. This sets up a contrast with the opinion that permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: So it seems / evidently (draws a conclusion)
To give a קינוי, the husband's warning to his wife not to be secluded with a certain man

phrases.english: Evidently, they hold
phrases.notes: 'They' means the opinions just quoted, which explained קינוי as a word of anger.

phrases.english: that it is forbidden to issue a warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from before this section, where קינוי was explained as a word of anger.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whoever reads קינוי as 'anger' holds that a husband is forbidden to give the warning.

steps.title: How does the permitting opinion read the word?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the opinion that permits giving the warning explains the word קינוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says it is permitted to give a warning, what does the word קינוי mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other opinion and asks a question. It is setting up the next step, where an answer will be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If קינוי means 'anger,' it is hard to say the warning is permitted. So the opinion that permits it must understand the word differently, and the גמרא wants to know how.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (the opinion that holds)
A term / a word that means

phrases.english: And according to the one who says it is permitted to issue a warning,
what is the meaning of the term 'kinnui'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר מוּתָּר לְקַנּאוֹת, מַהוּ לְשׁוֹן ״קִינּוּי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the forbidding opinion to the permitting one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the opinion that permits the warning understands the word קינוי.

steps.title: קינוי simply means a warning
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that קינוי means 'warning' and brings a פסוק from יואל as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: קינוי means nothing but a warning. As the פסוק says: 'And ה׳ warned (ויקנא) concerning His land.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question: the word קינוי just means 'warning,' and he shows the word used that way in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יואל‎, ה׳‎ 'ויקנא' for His land, meaning He gave a command or warning to protect it. So the root קנא can mean 'warn' and not only 'be angry.' On this reading, a husband's קינוי is just a warning, with nothing wrong in it, so it can be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says (introduces a supporting פסוק)
And He warned / showed concern (from the root קנא)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
'Kinnui' is nothing other than a term of warning,
and so it says:
'And the Lord warned concerning His land.'
phrases.notes: יואל 2:18

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֵין ״קִינּוּי״ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן הַתְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קינוי means 'warning,' as the root is used in יואל 2:18, so giving the warning is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument over whether a husband may give a קינוי depends on the meaning of the word: 'anger' leads to forbidden, while 'warning' leads to permitted.

steps.title: A secret sin is announced in public
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר teaches in a ברייתא that when a person sins in secret, הקדוש ברוך הוא announces it openly. He learns this from the word 'ועבר' in the סוטה פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי מאיר used to say, a person commits a sin in secret and הקדוש ברוך הוא announces it about him openly. As it says: 'And a spirit of jealousy passed (ועבר) upon him.' The word עבירה here means announcing, as it says: 'And משה commanded, and they announced (ויעבירו) throughout the camp.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a lesson from the סוטה פסוקים: a sin hidden in private ends up announced in public by ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads 'ועבר עליו רוח קנאה' as 'an announcement was made about him.' He proves that the root עבר can mean 'announce' from the פסוק where משה had a message 'passed through' the camp. The סוטה sinned in secret, yet the matter came out into the open.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Meir would say:
A person commits a transgression in private

phrases.aramaic: וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַכְרִיז עָלָיו בְּגָלוּי,
phrases.english: and the Holy One, Blessed be He, proclaims it about him openly,
as it is stated: 'And a spirit of jealousy passed upon him,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:14

phrases.english: and 'passing' is nothing other than a term of proclamation,
as it is stated: 'And Moses commanded,
and they caused a voice to pass through the camp.'
phrases.notes: שמות 36:6. Passing a voice through the camp means they announced it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, aggadic teaching based on the סוטה פסוקים, separate from the קינוי discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sin done in secret is publicized by הקדוש ברוך הוא, learned from reading ועבר as 'announcing.'
steps.confusionAlert: Here the word עבר is not read as 'transgress' or 'come over.' רבי מאיר reads it as 'announce,' like ויעבירו קול.

steps.title: Sin comes only from a spirit of foolishness
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that a person sins only when a spirit of foolishness enters him. He reads the word תשטה ('goes astray') as if it were written with a ש, connecting it to שטות.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: A person does not sin unless a spirit of foolishness enters him, as it says: 'Any man whose wife goes astray (תשטה).' The word is written so that it can be read תשטה, like שטות (foolishness).
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives another lesson from the סוטה פסוקים: sin happens only when a person loses his good sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תשטה is written with the letter ש. Without dots, that letter can be read as a shin, which ties the word to שטות, foolishness. So the פסוק itself hints that the woman's straying came from a moment of foolishness, and the same is true for anyone who sins.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes astray (the word as it is read)
It is written (how the word is spelled, not how it is read)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
A person does not commit a transgression

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְנַס בּוֹ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת,
phrases.english: unless a spirit of folly enters him,
as it is stated: 'Any man whose wife goes astray,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:12

phrases.english: it is written so it can be read 'tishteh.'
phrases.notes: The ש without dots can be read as a shin, which links the word to שטות, foolishness.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֵין אָדָם עוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְנַס בּוֹ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second aggadic lesson drawn from the סוטה פסוקים, alongside רבי מאיר's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sin comes only when a spirit of foolishness enters a person, hinted at in the spelling of תשטה.
steps.whatToRemember: Two lessons from the סוטה פסוקים: רבי מאיר teaches that a secret sin becomes public, and ריש לקיש teaches that sin comes from a moment of foolishness (שטות).

steps.title: Why one witness is believed about a סוטה
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that one witness is believed that a סוטה was defiled. This is because the warning and the seclusion already make the matter suspicious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Why did the Torah believe just one witness in the case of a סוטה? Because there is already a basis for suspicion. The husband warned her, she went and secluded herself anyway, and now one witness says she was defiled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא explaining why, in a סוטה case, one witness is enough to say she sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the Torah needs two witnesses. Here one is enough because the facts already point that way: she ignored her husband's warning (קינוי) and secluded herself (סתירה). The single witness only adds to a suspicion that already exists.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study hall) of רבי ישמעאל taught: introduces a ברייתא
Literally 'legs to the matter': there is a solid basis for suspicion
She secluded herself (with the man she was warned about)
Defiled: forbidden to her husband because she sinned

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא assumes the warning comes before the seclusion. רב פפא's challenge in the next step attacks exactly that assumption.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
For what reason did the Torah believe
a single witness in the case of a sotah?
Because there are 'legs' to the matter,
phrases.notes: He means there is already real ground for suspicion, so the witness isn't coming out of nowhere.

phrases.english: for he warned her, and she secluded herself,
and one witness testifies that she is defiled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the believability of one witness for a סוטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One witness is believed that a סוטה was defiled, because the earlier warning and her seclusion already create strong suspicion.

steps.title: The warning is written after the seclusion
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי: the פסוק mentions the warning only after seclusion and defilement, so how can the warning be the basis for suspicion?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But when the Torah writes about the warning, it writes it after the seclusion and the defilement!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the ברייתא's assumption that the warning came first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוקים, 'she was defiled in secret' comes first, and only then 'a spirit of jealousy came upon him, and he warned his wife.' That order suggests the warning comes after the sin. If so, the warning cannot be what makes the witness believable.

keyTerms.meaning: Seclusion: being alone with the man she was warned about

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But when the warning is written,
phrases.notes: He's pointing to במדבר 5:13–14.

phrases.english: it is written after the seclusion and the defilement!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: וְהָא כִּי כְּתִיבָה קִינּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order of events assumed in the ברייתא of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's assumption that the warning came before the seclusion and defilement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the פסוק, the warning is mentioned after seclusion and defilement, which suggests the warning comes later.

steps.title: ועבר means it had already happened
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the word ועבר in the פסוק means 'it had already come.' So the warning really happened earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: When the פסוק says 'And the spirit of jealousy came upon him,' it means it had already come upon him earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the ברייתא by reading one word in the פסוק as describing something that happened earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי admits the warning is written later in the פסוק. But he reads ועבר as past tense: the husband had already warned her before she secluded herself. So the Torah's order of writing is not the order of events.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it came (passed over)': the word from the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the פסוק is out of order by mistake. He is saying the word ועבר itself shows the warning had happened earlier.

phrases.english: He said to him:
'And it came' means: and it had already come.
phrases.notes: From במדבר 5:14, 'and the spirit of jealousy came upon him.' אביי reads it as something that already happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The order of the פסוק shows the warning came after the sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: ועבר means 'it had already come,' so the warning came before the seclusion.

steps.title: Challenge from the tribes crossing the ירדן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's reading. In another פסוק, ועבר clearly refers to the future, so the word cannot always mean 'already.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, when משה told the tribes of גד and ראובן, 'And every armed man of you will pass over,' does that also mean they had already crossed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's answer by showing the same word used about the future in a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was setting a condition about something that had not happened yet: the tribes still had to cross the ירדן. If ועבר means 'already happened,' that פסוק would make no sense. So the word alone cannot prove the warning came earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (from now on): pushes an idea to an absurd result
So too? Does it really mean that here as well?

phrases.english: But if that is so:
'And every armed man of you will pass over',
phrases.notes: במדבר 32:21

phrases.english: is it so here too, that they had already crossed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that ועבר means 'it had already come.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word is used in במדבר 32:21 about a future crossing, so it cannot automatically mean something already happened.

steps.title: The context decides what ועבר means
steps.stepSummary: In the פסוק about בני גד and בני ראובן, the words 'and afterward you shall return' show that ועבר is about the future. In the סוטה פסוק, reading ועבר as coming after defilement would make the warning pointless. So there it must mean 'already.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There, since it is written 'And the land be subdued before ה׳, and afterward you shall return,' it clearly means the future. But here, if you think the פסוקים are in the order they are written, with ועבר after the defilement and seclusion, why would I need a warning at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 9. It shows that the same word ועבר can point to the future in one place and to the past in another, depending on context.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said ועבר cannot always mean 'already.' The answer agrees, but says context decides. In במדבר 32 the next words ('afterward you shall return') force a future meaning. In the סוטה case, a warning given after she was already defiled and forbidden would do nothing, so ועבר must mean the warning came earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you were to think)
As they are written (in their written order)
The husband's warning to his wife not to be alone with a certain man
Seclusion: being alone with that man

steps.whatToRemember: ועבר does not have one fixed meaning. In the סוטה פסוק it means the warning already happened before the seclusion, so אביי's approach stands.

phrases.english: There, since it is written
"And the land be subdued before the Lord,
phrases.notes: במדבר 32:22

phrases.english: and afterward you shall return"
it clearly means the future.
But here,
if you think the verses go in the order they are written,
so that "ve'avar" comes after the defilement and seclusion,
why do I need a warning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by separating the two uses of ועבר based on context.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ועבר always has the same meaning, so if it means future in במדבר 32 it cannot mean 'already' here.
steps.terutzMaskana: In במדבר 32 the context shows the future. In the סוטה פסוק the warning would be pointless after defilement, so ועבר means 'already.'

steps.title: A husband warns his wife only when a spirit enters him
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that a man gives his wife a קינוי only if a 'spirit' has entered him, based on the words 'a spirit of jealousy came upon him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: A man does not warn his wife unless a spirit has entered him, as it says: 'And a spirit of jealousy came upon him, and he warned his wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about the קינוי from the same פסוק. Something has to stir the husband before he warns his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the word רוח in the פסוק. The warning is described as coming from a 'spirit' that passed over the husband. The teaching leaves open what kind of spirit this is, and the next step asks exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
A man does not warn his wife

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְנְסָה בּוֹ רוּחַ,
phrases.english: unless a spirit has entered him,
as it says:
"And a spirit of jealousy came upon him
and he warned his wife."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new teaching based on the same סוטה פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband warns his wife only when a 'spirit' has entered him.

steps.title: What kind of spirit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the 'spirit' in דבי רבי ישמעאל's teaching is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What spirit is meant?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step. It wants to know whether this spirit is a good thing or a bad thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רוח could mean a positive push or a negative one. The answer will decide whether warning one's wife is a worthy act or an unfortunate one.

phrases.english: What spirit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the word רוח in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the spirit that moves the husband to warn is an impure spirit or a pure one.

steps.title: Spirit of impurity or spirit of purity
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say it is a רוח טומאה. רב אשי says it is a רוח טהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן say: a spirit of impurity. רב אשי says: a spirit of purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two opposite answers to the question. One view sees the warning as coming from something negative, the other from something positive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the urge to warn comes from a bad spirit, so it is not a desirable act. For רב אשי, it comes from a pure spirit, a husband who will not put up with improper behavior. The next step will decide between them.

phrases.english: The Rabbis say: a spirit of impurity.
Rav Ashi says: a spirit of purity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן: a spirit of impurity. רב אשי: a spirit of purity.

steps.title: Proof that it is a spirit of purity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רב אשי from a ברייתא. רבי ישמעאל says warning is optional and רבי עקיבא says it is obligatory. The Torah would never make bringing a spirit of impurity into yourself optional or required.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense like the one who says 'spirit of purity.' A ברייתא teaches: 'And he warned his wife' is optional, says רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says it is obligatory. If it is a spirit of purity, that works. But if it is a spirit of impurity, could it be optional or obligatory for a person to bring a spirit of impurity into himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that רב אשי's view, a spirit of purity, makes more sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions in the ברייתא treat the warning as allowed or even required. Neither calls it forbidden. That fits a pure spirit, but it cannot fit an impure one, because the Torah would not permit or require someone to bring impurity into himself. So the רוח must be a רוח טהרה.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'spirit' that moves a husband to warn his wife is a רוח טהרה. Since warning is either optional (רבי ישמעאל) or obligatory (רבי עקיבא), it cannot come from a spirit of impurity.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof does not rest on רבי ישמעאל alone. Neither רבי ישמעאל ('optional') nor רבי עקיבא ('required') says that warning is forbidden. That only fits a spirit of purity.

phrases.english: And it stands to reason
like the one who says a spirit of purity.
As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And he warned his wife": this is optional,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says: it is obligatory.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא רוּחַ טׇהֳרָה — שַׁפִּיר,
phrases.english: Granted, if you say a spirit of purity, that works well,
but if you say a spirit of impurity,
could it be optional or obligatory
for a person to bring a spirit of impurity into himself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opinions of step 13 in favor of רב אשי.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's view that the spirit is a רוח טהרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל calls warning optional and רבי עקיבא calls it obligatory. Neither could be said about bringing impurity into oneself.

steps.title: The full ברייתא: three optional-or-required disputes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא it just used and quotes it in full. רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue in the same way about three פסוקים: warning one's wife, a כהן becoming impure for his sister, and keeping a slave forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the ברייתא itself: 'And he warned his wife' is optional, says רבי ישמעאל; רבי עקיבא says it is required. 'For her he may become impure' is optional, says רבי ישמעאל; רבי עקיבא says it is required. 'Forever you shall work with them' is optional, says רבי ישמעאל; רבי עקיבא says it is required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to study the ברייתא from step 14 on its own and quotes all of it. It turns out the same disagreement shows up in three different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 only the first dispute, about the warning, was needed as a proof. Now we see the full ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל calls all three actions optional, and רבי עקיבא calls all three required. This repeating pattern sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself.' The גמרא returns to study a source it quoted earlier
Optional. You may do it, but you don't have to
'For her he may become impure.' A כהן becoming טמא to bury his sister
A non-Jewish slave. The פסוק says to keep him 'forever'

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. רבי ישמעאל says 'optional' every time, and רבי עקיבא says 'required' every time.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: We're going back to the ברייתא from step 14 to learn the whole thing.

phrases.english: 'And he warned his wife' — is optional,
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:14

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
And Rabbi Akiva says: it is mandatory.
'For her he may become impure' — is optional,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:3. This is about a כהן becoming impure to bury his sister.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
And Rabbi Akiva says: it is mandatory.
'Forever you shall work with them' — is optional,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:46. This is about keeping a non-Jewish slave forever instead of freeing him.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says: it is mandatory.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא that step 14 used as a proof, now quoting it fully to study it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In three places (קינוי, a כהן's impurity for his sister, keeping a עבד כנעני forever), רבי ישמעאל says רשות and רבי עקיבא says חובה.

steps.title: Do they argue this way throughout the whole Torah?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא (or רב משרשיא) asks whether רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא have one general disagreement everywhere in the Torah, with one always saying optional and the other always saying required.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי (some say רב משרשיא said to רבא): Shall we say that רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue this way about the entire Torah, with one saying 'optional' and the other saying 'required'?
steps.whatsHappening: Seeing the same pattern three times, an אמורא asks whether this is really one big general argument between these two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the answer were yes, then wherever a פסוק is unclear about being optional or required, we would know ahead of time how each תנא rules. The question checks whether the pattern is a general rule or just a coincidence of these three cases.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall we say...?' Introduces a suggestion the גמרא is testing
'One master... and the other master.' One side and the other side
'And some say.' A second version of who said it

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye,
and some say it was Rav Mesharshiya to Rava:
Shall we say that Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva
disagree this way throughout the entire Torah,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר אָמַר רְשׁוּת וּמָר אָמַר חוֹבָה?
phrases.english: that one master says optional and the other master says mandatory?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ הָכִי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notices the repeated pattern in the ברייתא and asks whether it is one general disagreement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא hold a general, Torah-wide position that unclear commands are optional or required.

steps.title: No, each dispute comes from its own פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The answer: there is no general rule. In these cases they disagree about how to read each specific פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Here they disagree about the verses themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered. The two תנאים are not following one big rule. Each argument comes from how they read that particular פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three disputes look alike, but each has its own reason based on the wording of its own פסוק. So we cannot use this pattern to guess their opinions about other places in the Torah. This also tells us the גמרא now has to explain each פסוק separately.
steps.whatToRemember: The disputes between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא over רשות and חובה are not one general rule. Each comes from reading its own פסוק.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Here they disagree about the verses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by denying a general rule and tying each dispute to its own פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They do not have a Torah-wide dispute. In each case here, they disagree about the reading of that specific פסוק.

steps.title: Going back to the first פסוק: the warning
steps.stepSummary: Since each dispute depends on its own פסוק, the גמרא starts going through them one at a time. It re-quotes the first one, about warning one's wife, to explain each side's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he warned his wife' is optional, says רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says it is required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It repeats the first dispute so it can now explain where each side gets its view from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not just repetition. Step 17 said each argument comes from its own פסוק, so now the גמרא has to show that reading for each one. It begins with the warning, the main topic of מסכת סוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he warned.' The husband's warning to his wife about secluding with a certain man
'The words of.' Marks whose opinion this is

phrases.english: 'And he warned his wife' — is optional,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says: it is mandatory.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקִנֵּא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ רְשׁוּת דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Following the answer that each dispute depends on its own פסוק, this re-quotes the first dispute to begin explaining it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: About the warning (קינוי), רבי ישמעאל says it is רשות and רבי עקיבא says it is חובה. Each side's reasoning from the פסוק will follow.

steps.title: What is רבי ישמעאל's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל holds that warning one's wife is only optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי ישמעאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי ישמעאל's view that קינוי is optional. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said each dispute depends on how the specific פסוק is read. So the גמרא now asks which reading of the פסוק makes רבי ישמעאל say 'optional.'

keyTerms.meaning: Optional, permitted but not required (רבי ישמעאל's view)

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yishmael?
phrases.notes: He is the one who said warning one's wife is optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the first dispute that step 18 re-quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק-based source for רבי ישמעאל's view that קינוי is optional.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: the warning is only permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל agrees with a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. It says the פסוק 'וקנא את אשתו' comes to permit the warning, so the husband is not breaking the איסור of hating in one's heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, since the Torah said 'Do not hate your brother in your heart,' I might think it applies even in a case like this. So the פסוק says: 'And a spirit of jealousy came over him and he warned his wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. The words 'וקנא את אשתו' come to tell us the husband is allowed to warn his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this פסוק, we might think a husband who sees his wife acting improperly must keep quiet, because of 'לא תשנא את אחיך בלבבך.' The פסוק removes that worry and says warning her is allowed. Something that is only 'allowed' is optional, not required.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not hate your brother in your heart (ויקרא 19:17)
A teacher from the time of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי ישמעאל means the Torah is lukewarm about the warning. The פסוק is written to permit it, so that no one thinks it is forbidden. That is why it ends up optional.

phrases.english: He holds like this tanna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
Regarding what the Torah said,
"Do not hate your brother in your heart,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:17

phrases.english: might I think it applies even in a case like this?
phrases.notes: He means a husband who sees his wife acting improperly with another man. Maybe he should keep his feelings to himself?

phrases.english: So the verse says:
"And a spirit of jealousy came over him
and he warned his wife."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:14

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וקנא את אשתו' comes to permit the warning despite 'לא תשנא,' so קינוי is only optional.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: a second warning is written
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns that the warning is required, because the פסוק mentions 'וקנא את אשתו' a second time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא? Another warning is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי עקיבא's source. The פסוק says 'he warned his wife' twice: one mention permits the warning and the other makes it required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא agrees that the first mention only permits it. But a second mention would be extra unless it teaches more, so he reads it as making the warning a חובה.

keyTerms.meaning: The husband's warning to his wife not to be alone with a certain man

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva — how does he learn it is required?
Another warning is written.
phrases.notes: The same פסוק says 'and he warned his wife' a second time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the dispute, after רבי ישמעאל's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second 'וקנא' in the פסוק makes the warning required.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: the second warning is there only because of 'defiled' and 'not defiled'
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל explains that the second 'וקנא' is not an extra teaching. It is written only because the Torah needed to spell out both cases, 'she was defiled' and 'she was not defiled.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל? Since the Torah needed to write 'and she was defiled' and 'and she was not defiled,' it also wrote 'and he warned his wife' again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי ישמעאל deals with the second warning in the פסוק. It answers that the repetition is just part of writing out the second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes two cases: one where she was defiled and one where she was not. When the Torah writes out the second case, it repeats the whole description, including 'וקנא.' So for רבי ישמעאל the repeated word adds no new law, and the warning stays optional.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael — what does he do with the second warning?
Since it needed to write
"and she was defiled"
and "and she was not defiled" —
it also wrote "and he warned his wife."
phrases.notes: The second case repeats the whole opening, so the warning shows up again along with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי ישמעאל against רבי עקיבא's proof from the second 'וקנא.'
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's view that קינוי is optional
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק writes 'וקנא' twice, which seems to teach that the warning is required.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The repetition is a byproduct of writing out the second case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second 'וקנא' is an extra word that teaches חובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is written only because the Torah spelled out the 'not defiled' case in full.

steps.title: Support from the school of רבי ישמעאל: a repeated passage is repeated only for its new detail
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל's reading matches a rule taught in his school: when a Torah passage is said and then repeated, the repetition is only for the new detail it adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Every passage that was said and then repeated was repeated only for the new thing added in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי ישמעאל's answer with a general rule from his own school about repeated passages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the Torah repeats a passage to add one new point, the old parts that come along with it are not extra teachings. Here the new point is 'she was not defiled,' so the repeated 'וקנא' does not make the warning a חובה.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל: 'וקנא' only permits the warning, and its second mention comes along with the 'not defiled' case, so קינוי is רשות. רבי עקיבא: the second 'וקנא' teaches חובה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule about repeated passages is a general tool for reading the Torah. It explains why the same words can show up twice without teaching two separate laws.

phrases.english: This is like what the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught.
For the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Every passage that was said and then repeated —
was repeated only
for the new thing added in it.
phrases.notes: Here the new thing is 'she was not defiled.' The repeated warning just comes along with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 22 with a general reading rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ישמעאל's claim that the second 'וקנא' teaches nothing new
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל: a repeated passage is repeated only for its new detail.

steps.title: The second dispute: is becoming impure for a relative optional or required?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second dispute of the ברייתא. For 'לה יטמא', רבי ישמעאל says it is רשות and רבי עקיבא says it is חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says about a כהן's sister: 'For her may he become impure.' רבי ישמעאל says this is optional. רבי עקיבא says it is required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the second argument from the ברייתא so it can now explain it. This line sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן is normally forbidden to become טמא from a dead body, but the Torah lets him do so for close relatives. The argument is whether he only may do it (רבי ישמעאל) or must do it (רבי עקיבא). It has the same pattern as the first argument about warning one's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For her may he become impure': the פסוק allowing a כהן to become טמא for his sister
'The words of'; this is the opinion of

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a second example of the same disagreement in method: does a repeated or extra פסוק add a new law, or is it written only because the context needed it?

phrases.english: "For her may he become impure" is optional.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:3. It is about a כהן helping to bury his sister even though he becomes טמא.

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says: it is mandatory.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָהּ יִטַּמָּא רְשׁוּת דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first dispute (warning one's wife) to the second dispute in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: a כהן becoming טמא for his relative is optional. רבי עקיבא: it is required.

steps.title: What is the reason of רבי ישמעאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל reads 'לה יטמא' as only permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי ישמעאל's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל thinks the פסוק only gives permission. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לה יטמא' sound like a command, so we need to know why רבי ישמעאל reads them as mere permission. The question looks for the purpose these words serve in his view.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yishmael?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source and reasoning behind רבי ישמעאל's opinion in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי ישמעאל reads 'לה יטמא' as only רשות and not חובה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: the verse was needed to permit what was forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The Torah first forbade a כהן to become טמא for the dead. So it had to write 'לה יטמא' to allow it for a relative. The words are only a permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah wrote, 'Speak to the כהנים... none shall become impure for the dead among his people.' After that, it had to write 'For her may he become impure' to tell us it is allowed for a relative.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the words 'לה יטמא' come only to lift the general איסור for a relative. They do not create an obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the Torah set a ban on a כהן becoming טמא, saying 'he may become impure for her' simply makes an exception. Something that undoes an איסור naturally means 'allowed,' not 'required.' This matches how רבי ישמעאל read 'וקנא' in step 20, as a permission.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is written; because the Torah already wrote
He shall not become impure for a dead person

phrases.english: Since it is written:
"Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:1

phrases.english: and say to them:
none shall become impure for the dead among his people,"
it was necessary to write "For her may he become impure."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the Torah forbade a כהן to become טמא for the dead, 'לה יטמא' was needed only to allow it for a relative. So it is רשות.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: permission is already known, so the extra words make it required
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns the permission from the earlier פסוק 'כי אם לשארו'. So the extra words 'לה יטמא' must teach that it is a חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא? He already learns the permission from 'except for his kin.' So why does the Torah need 'For her may he become impure'? To make it required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי עקיבא answers רבי ישמעאל's reasoning. The permission is already written earlier, so 'לה יטמא' must add something new: an obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל said 'לה יטמא' was needed for permission. רבי עקיבא answers that 'כי אם לשארו' already gave that permission. Since the Torah does not repeat for nothing, the second phrase must teach a חובה, just as he read the second 'וקנא' in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Except for his kin': the earlier פסוק allowing a כהן to become טמא for relatives
He derives it; he learns it from
Why do I need it? (what does this extra wording teach?)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva?
He derives the permission from "except for his kin."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:2

phrases.english: Why do I need "For her may he become impure"?
To make it mandatory.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מִכִּי אִם לִשְׁאֵרוֹ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי עקיבא's view and pushes back on step 26's claim that 'לה יטמא' was needed for permission.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Permission comes from 'כי אם לשארו', so 'לה יטמא' is extra and teaches חובה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: the extra words exclude becoming impure for just a limb
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל uses the extra 'לה' to teach that a כהן becomes טמא for his relative's whole body, but not for only one of her limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל? He learns: for her, her whole body, he becomes impure. But he does not become impure for her limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי ישמעאל: he also sees the extra words, but he uses them for a different law. They limit the permission to a complete body, not a single limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's challenge was that the extra phrase must teach something. רבי ישמעאל agrees it teaches something, but not a חובה. The word 'לה' (for her) limits the permission to the whole person and leaves out a lone limb.
steps.whatToRemember: In both disputes (warning one's wife, and becoming impure for a relative), רבי ישמעאל reads the words as permission. רבי עקיבא reads the extra words as making it required. Here רבי ישמעאל uses the extra words for a separate detail: a whole body, not a limb.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael?
phrases.notes: He means: what does רבי ישמעאל do with the extra words "לה יטמא"?

phrases.english: For her he becomes impure,
phrases.notes: "Her" means her whole body.

phrases.english: but he does not become impure for her limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לָהּ מִיטַּמֵּא וְאֵין מִיטַּמֵּא לְאֵיבָרֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pressure from step 27 by giving the extra words a different purpose in רבי ישמעאל's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the extra phrase to teach a different law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'לה יטמא' looks extra after 'כי אם לשארו', one might think it must teach חובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'לה' teaches that the permission covers only a whole body and not a single limb, so it can still be only רשות.
